name: mosml
why: Moscow ML is an old Standard ML implementation with a retro functional-language flavour that rewards an afternoon of exploration.

brief.what_it_is: Moscow ML is a lightweight implementation of Standard ML (SML), a strict functional language. It provides an interactive top-level system and a batch compiler, and it reads SML source files and produces bytecode, or compact stand-alone executables. It implements the full language as revised in 1997, including modules, and large parts of the SML Basis Library. The distribution also includes lex and yacc style tools (mosmllex, mosmlyac) and a bytecode runtime (camlrunm).
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage describes it as a light-weight implementation of Standard ML used in teaching and research. The README says it is written to be backwards compatible with versions before 2.00 and to match the 1997 SML revision.
brief.how_it_works: The README says the bytecode generator and runtime system come from the Caml Light implementation by Xavier Leroy and Damien Doligez. It supports separate compilation and can produce compact stand-alone executables in the style of Caml Light. It also supports dynamic linking of external functions on several platforms, and quotations and antiquotations for metaprogramming.
brief.install_notes: Neither the homepage nor the README gives a brew-specific command. The README says compiling under Unix is best done with GNU make, gcc and Perl. Disk space is 25 MB for a source install; the homepage says 5 MB for binary and the README says 8 MB. Official routes are: build from source (GitHub releases or the zipball), an Ubuntu PPA, a Mac OS X 10.9 .pkg installer that installs to /usr/local, or a Windows installer made by Sebastian Paaske Tørholm (Eckankar). Installation instructions are in install.txt in the source tree.
brief.standout: It is a small, old Standard ML system with a Caml Light runtime heritage, shipping separate compilation, stand-alone executables and quotation/antiquotation support. That makes it an unusual place to meet SML outside the usual SML/NJ or MLton ecosystems.
brief.status: quiet. The current version is 2.10.1, and the README header is dated August 2014. The homepage says it moved to GitHub development, but I did not see commit dates or a newer release, so I cannot say more than that.
brief.caveats: The docs are for version 2.10, and the platform list (including Windows 95 to Vista, and Linux x86, ARM and Alpha) is old. The README says it is GPL v2 or later. It also warns that charging money for redistribution may need prior permission from INRIA because some files derive from Caml Light. Building from source is the main route, and the README mentions a dependency on GNU make, gcc and Perl. I did not see any usage commands in either page.
quotes: Moscow ML is a light-weight implementation of Standard ML (SML), a strict functional language used in teaching and research
implements the full Standard ML language, as revised 1997, including Modules and some extensions
can produce compact stand-alone executables (a la Caml Light)
Moscow ML is now developed in the open at github.
